subtitle: A shared spring-applied platform
description: A fixed opposed-pad bridge concept around the common 400 mm disc. A purchased spring-applied hydraulic-release cartridge is represented by its envelope; its internal mechanism is not designed here.
targets: Concept area before corner / retention detail
decisions: A fixed bridge establishes a direct load path; removable pad retainers are a serviceability hypothesis.
Use a bought release cartridge for the first test rig rather than developing seals and spring stacks simultaneously.
Share the rotor/hub pattern with the positive-actuated brake study.
materials: Bridge and cheeks: S355J2+N plate for prototype; machined critical faces after fabrication.
Pad backing: C45 steel candidate, with purchased qualified lining.
Tie fasteners: purchased certified fasteners; grade, preload and locking method unresolved.
risks: Bridge deflection, pad pressure distribution and hot clearance are not verified.
Cartridge load path and equalization are interface requirements, not functional geometry.
Pressure, spring force and release stroke must come from the selected supplier.
steps: Locate bridge and cheek plates with interface holes aligned.
Install replaceable backing plates, lining and retainer pins.
Mount supplier-approved actuator cartridges on the outer interfaces.
Centre rotor in the cold gap; verify hot-growth allowance analytically.
Approve joint preload, retainer security and release stroke before guarded testing.
validation: Contact/nonlinear bridge FEA with supplier actuator loads.
Thermal distortion, wear travel and worst-case tolerance stack.
Torque versus pressure/release state, pad change, leakage and endurance tests.
hypotheses: Timed pad change with matched guarding and access.
Demonstrate common disc and hub across two actuation variants.
sensors: Advisory position / wear sensing with replaceable brackets; no AI-controlled brake release.
Record supplier sensor range, supply, connector, EMC, ingress and temperature limits before selection.
Define independent machine safety interface and diagnostic fault response with the responsible controls engineer.
